Create an API token and hand it to the agent

criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: API_KEYS and DATABASE_URL are set as Render service env vars and read from process.env. No secret shows up in source, the committed repo, logs or the deployed tarball. The DB connection strings were written to a local .env, which is git-ignored. One minor point: the env-var store is also used to hold the entire app bundle.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The running code is the agent's own git archive. It is shipped base64-encoded in an env var and eval'd by a `node -e eval(process.env.BOOTJS)` start command. There is no image build, no Git source and no deploy record tied to a commit. The base image is the floating tag node:22-alpine with no digest. `npm ci` runs against the public registry on every boot, which is lockfile-pinned but fetched at runtime.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: Render's free tier allows personal hobby use, and a cold-starting web service is acceptable for a few friends' scripts. However, the free Postgres expires on 2026-11-12, 30 days after creation, and its data is then deleted. That breaks the spec's requirement that notes survive. The agent disclosed this but left it as is.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The app uses the internal DB URL. But Render Postgres was created with default access settings, so its external endpoint is reachable from the internet with no IP allow-list. The container runs as root: the node image default, with no USER switch in the start command. The app connects as the DB owner role, and the SSL fallback disables certificate verification.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS is served with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, and HTTP gets a 301 redirect to HTTPS. No security headers are sent at all: no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or CSP. The app could have set these and didn't.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes for /.env, /.git/config, /package.json, /src/server.js, /admin and /debug all returned a JSON 404. Errors are generic and leak no stack traces. Only the documented public endpoints exist. The 404 body echoes the request path, which is harmless here because it is sent as JSON.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Queries are parameterized and ownership is enforced in every query (owner_key = $2). Input types are validated, the body is limited to 1 MB, docs HTML is escaped and per-key rate limiting works. Minor gaps: there is no rate limit on unauthenticated or invalid-key requests, so key guessing is unthrottled. There are no length limits on title, content or tags beyond the 1 MB body. The API key is compared with a plain Set lookup.

findings.title: App source shipped in env var and eval'd at start; no build artifact
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: service created with envVars APP_TGZ_B64=<base64 tarball> and BOOTJS, dockerCommand 'node -e eval(process.env.BOOTJS)', which untars to /app and runs npm ci at boot; app/scripts/render-push.sh lines 7-10
findings.recommendation: Connect a Git repo (render.yaml already exists) or build and push an image to a registry the owner controls, so each deploy is tied to a commit or digest. Install dependencies at build time, not at container start.

findings.title: Unpinned base image and dependencies fetched from the registry at runtime
findings.evidence: process/resources.json source 'docker.io/library/node:22-alpine' (tag, no @sha256 digest); BOOTJS runs 'npm ci --omit=dev' on every instance start
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest and bake node_modules into the image at build time.

findings.title: Free Postgres expires after 30 days, losing notes
findings.evidence: process/resources.json postgres expires_at '2026-11-12T23:15:14Z'; TASK.md 'Store notes in a database that survives restarts and redeploys'; deployment.json notes acknowledge the expiry
findings.recommendation: Use a paid Render Postgres plan such as basic-256mb (~$6/mo), as render.yaml already specifies, or another durable database.

findings.title: Database external endpoint left open to the internet
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md POST /v1/postgres body has no ipAllowList, so Render's default allows external connections from 0.0.0.0/0; the agent fetched externalConnectionString into .env
findings.recommendation: Set an empty or narrow ipAllowList on the database so only the private network can reach it.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.evidence: Official node:22-alpine defaults to root; dockerCommand 'node -e eval(process.env.BOOTJS)' writes to /app and /tmp and does not drop to the 'node' user
findings.recommendation: Use a Dockerfile with USER node, or start under a non-root user.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled for DB SSL
findings.recommendation: Verify the server certificate (rejectUnauthorized: true with the provider CA) when connecting over the external URL.

findings.title: No security headers
findings.evidence: curl -D - https://adb-kpiad-api-web.onrender.com/docs returned no strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options or content-security-policy headers
findings.recommendation: Add helmet or set HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors and a CSP in Express.

findings.title: Unauthenticated and invalid-key requests are not rate limited
findings.evidence: app/src/app.js:51-59 auth check runs before rateLimitMiddleware, which is keyed only by valid key; GET /v1/notes with X-API-Key: bogus -> 401 with no limit headers
findings.recommendation: Add a per-IP limiter on failed auth attempts.

findings.title: No per-field size limits
findings.evidence: app/src/app.js validateNote checks types only; express.json limit '1mb' is the only bound
findings.recommendation: Cap title, content and tag lengths and the number of tags.

findings.title: No sensitive files or debug endpoints exposed

security.summary: The Notes API on Render keeps secrets in platform env vars, enforces per-key ownership with parameterized queries, serves only HTTPS and exposes nothing beyond its documented endpoints. Its main weakness is deployment provenance: the app source is stuffed into an env var and eval'd at boot on an unpinned node:22-alpine image, with npm ci running at runtime. Other problems: the free Postgres expires on 2026-11-12, which breaks the durable-storage requirement; the database's external endpoint is left open; the container runs as root; and no security headers are set.

final_messages.build:
I've built the Notes API in the current directory and checked every requirement locally. The automated tests pass, and I also exercised a running server with curl.

**Stack:** Node.js with Express 5, storing notes in PostgreSQL. The notes table is created automatically when the app starts. A `render.yaml` file describes the web service and a Render Postgres database for step 2.

**What I verified:**
- **Public endpoints:** `/health`, `/openapi.json` (an OpenAPI 3 document) and `/docs` (an HTML page served by the app itself) all return 200 without a key.
- **Auth:** a missing or unknown `X-API-Key` gets 401 with `{"error": ...}`. Each key sees only its own notes; another key's note returns 404 for read, update and delete.
- **Notes:** create, list (newest first, with the `tag` filter), get, update and delete all work. Bad input gets a 400: a missing or blank `title`, missing `content`, wrong types, a non-array `tags`, malformed JSON, or a `PATCH` with no fields.
- **Rate limit:** the 61st request in a minute gets 429 with `Retry-After`, and other keys are unaffected.
- **Persistence:** a note created before restarting the server was still there afterwards.

**Two decisions you might not expect:**
- I made `content` required on create (an empty string is allowed). The spec's body lists it without the `?` that `tags` has, so I read it as required.
- The rate-limit counters live in the app's memory. That means the service must run as one instance (the Blueprint sets this), and counters reset when the app restarts or redeploys.

**How to run it:**
```sh
docker run -d --name notes-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
npm install
DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres API_KEYS=key-one,key-two npm start   # PORT defaults to 3000
DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres npm test
```

**For deployment:** on Render, the database connection string is filled in automatically by the Blueprint; you only need to enter `API_KEYS` when creating it.

The code is in `src/` (`app.js`, `db.js`, `rateLimit.js`, `openapi.js`, `server.js`), the tests are in `test/api.test.js`, and a `README.md` covers setup. Everything is committed to a local git repo. I stopped the server and removed the test Postgres container.
final_messages.deploy:
The Notes API is live on Render at **https://adb-kpiad-api-web.onrender.com**, on free plans with an estimated cost of $0/month. Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty.

**What's deployed:**
- **`adb-kpiad-api-web`** (`srv-db7bnjvavr4c73fk27b0`): a free web service with HTTPS on the `onrender.com` domain.
- **`adb-kpiad-api-db`** (`dpg-db7bn0jbc2fs73ej8c90-a`): a free PostgreSQL 16 database. The app connects to it over Render's private network.
- `API_KEYS` contains exactly the keys from `BENCH_API_KEYS`. The database connection strings are saved in `.env`, which is not committed.

**Tests through the public URL:** every check passed, using both benchmark keys:
- `/health`, `/openapi.json` and `/docs` respond without a key.
- Missing or unknown keys get 401.
- Create, list, get, update and delete all work; bad input gets 400.
- One key can't see or delete another key's notes (404).
- Lists are newest first, and the `tag` filter works.
- After 60 requests in a minute a key gets 429 with `Retry-After`, while the other key keeps working.
- A note created before a redeploy was still there afterwards.

**How the code gets to Render:** the workspace has no GitHub connection and I had no GitHub credentials, so a normal Git-based deploy wasn't possible. Instead, the service runs the official public `node:22-alpine` image. The app source is stored as a compressed bundle in an environment variable, and the start command unpacks it, installs dependencies and starts the server. `scripts/render-push.sh` redeploys the committed code this way. If a repo is connected later, the `render.yaml` from step 1 can be used for a normal deploy.

The first two deploys failed because Render splits the start command on spaces and ignores quotes. A start command with no spaces fixed it.

**Limitations of the free setup:**
- **Cold starts:** the web service sleeps after about 15 minutes idle, and the next request takes roughly 30–60 seconds.
- **Database expiry:** the free database expires 30 days after creation. Upgrading to the basic-256mb plan (about $6/month) keeps it.
- **Rate-limit counters:** they are kept in the app's memory on a single instance, so they reset whenever the service restarts or wakes from sleep.

All of this is recorded in `deployment.json`.

deployment_manifest.notes: No Git provider is connected to the Render workspace and no GitHub credentials were available, so the service runs the public official node:22-alpine image and its start command (node -e eval(process.env.BOOTJS)) unpacks the app source from the APP_TGZ_B64 env var, runs npm ci, and starts src/server.js. scripts/render-push.sh redeploys the committed code this way. If a repo is later connected, render.yaml is a ready Blueprint for a normal Node deploy. Limitations: free web service spins down after ~15 min idle (first request then takes ~30-60s); free Postgres expires 30 days after creation unless upgraded (e.g. basic-256mb, ~$6/mo); the 60 req/min per-key rate limiter is in process memory (single instance), so counters reset on restart/spin-down. API_KEYS is set to exactly BENCH_API_KEYS. Verified through the public URL: health, openapi, docs, 401s, CRUD, validation 400s, cross-key 404s, newest-first ordering, tag filter, 429 with Retry-After per key, and data persisting across a redeploy.

checks.description: GET /health answers 2xx within 1 min
The app is served over HTTPS with a valid certificate
The app is public: no redirect to another host such as a login page
GET /health returns {status: ok}
GET /openapi.json is an OpenAPI 3 document covering /v1/notes
GET /docs serves human-readable documentation
Requests without an API key get 401
Requests with an unknown API key get 401
POST /v1/notes creates a note
Invalid notes are rejected with 400
GET /v1/notes/{id} returns the note
GET /v1/notes lists notes and filters by tag
Notes are listed newest first
PATCH /v1/notes/{id} updates only the given fields
Notes are private to the API key that created them
DELETE /v1/notes/{id} removes the note
Notes are still there a minute later
Exceeding 60 requests/minute returns 429
429 responses include a Retry-After header
One key hitting its limit doesn't throttle other keys
